subtopics.name: Strategies for Managing Impacts of Tectonic Events

parts.problem_md:
Volcanic activity provides opportunities for people.

State three of these opportunities.
parts.solution_md:
> **[mark-scheme]**
> Any **three** from:
> 
> - Fertile soils for farming
> - Extraction of minerals
> - Building materials
> - Geothermal power
> - Tourism
> 
> **[3 marks]**

parts.problem_md:
During volcanic eruptions, magma rises to the surface to form lava.

Name two other substances emitted from volcanoes.
parts.solution_md:
> **[mark-scheme]**
> Any **two** from:
> 
> - Ash
> - Volcanic bombs
> - Water vapour
> - Carbon dioxide
> - Sulfur dioxide
> - Pyroclastic flows
> 
> **[2 marks]**

parts.problem_md:
Table 4.1 compares two volcanic eruptions, A and B, in 2010.

**Table 4.1**

| volcanic eruption | A | B |
|---|---|---|
| country | Iceland | Indonesia |
| location | Eyjafjallajökull | Mount Merapi |
| number of deaths | 0 | 353 |
| VEI value | 4 | 4 |
| world bank classification of country | HIC | MIC |

Suggest why the number of deaths from eruption A was lower than the number of deaths from eruption B.
parts.solution_md:
Iceland is an HIC, so it has more money to spend on preparing for eruptions than Indonesia, an MIC  **[1 mark]**. Iceland can monitor its volcanoes to predict eruptions  **[1 mark]** and has early warning systems  **[1 mark]**, so people can be evacuated in time  **[1 mark]**. More people may live close to Mount Merapi than close to Eyjafjallajökull  **[1 mark]**.

> **[mark-scheme]**
> **Mark allocation**
> 
> This answer is assessed using a point-marked approach.
> 
> - One mark for each valid point
> - Maximum 5 marks
> 
> **Alternative content**
> 
> The answer above is just one example of how to respond to this question. Other information that could be used includes:
> 
> - Iceland has disaster plans and holds drills
> - Iceland can provide emergency supplies such as water, shelter and medical supplies
> - Iceland has trained rescue teams
> - The eruptions may have happened at different times of day
> - Victims of eruption B may have been harder to reach
> - Any other suitable response
> 
> **Common errors**
> 
> - Saying eruption A was smaller: both eruptions had a VEI of 4

> **[exam-tip]**
> - Use the table. Both eruptions had the same VEI, so the difference comes from the countries, not the size of the eruptions.

parts.problem_md:
The volcanic explosivity index, VEI, is a measure of the explosiveness of volcanic eruptions.

A VEI value of 0 is the least explosive and a VEI value of 8 is the most explosive.

Figure 4.2 shows the VEI value for some eruptions around the world.

![Bar chart of number of eruptions against VEI, showing VEI 2–7 on the horizontal axis and zero to 4,000 eruptions on the vertical axis. ](assets/001-bar-chart-of-number-of-eruptions-against-vei-sho.png)

*Figure 4.2*

Describe what Figure 4.2 shows about these volcanic eruptions.
parts.solution_md:
As the VEI increases, the number of eruptions decreases  **[1 mark]**. VEI 2 eruptions are the most common, at about 3500, and VEI 7 eruptions are the rarest  **[1 mark]**.

> **[exam-tip]**
> - Describe the overall pattern first, then support it with figures from the highest or lowest bar.

parts.problem_md:
Iceland is situated on the Mid-Atlantic Ridge plate boundary.

Figure 4.1 shows the plates, the Mid-Atlantic Ridge and the location of Iceland's major volcanoes.

![Map of Iceland showing the Mid-Atlantic Ridge, major volcanoes and plate movement. The grey ridge separates the North American and Eurasian plates, with arrows moving apart; symbols mark the capital city and volcanoes including Eyjafjallajökull and Surtsey.](assets/002-map-of-iceland-showing-the-mid-atlantic-ridge-ma.png)

*Figure 4.1*

Use Figure 4.1 to describe the distribution of major volcanoes in Iceland.
parts.solution_md:
Most of the major volcanoes lie on the Mid-Atlantic Ridge  **[1 mark]**. Seven volcanoes are on the ridge and three are not  **[1 mark]**. More volcanoes are in the southern half of the island than in the north  **[1 mark]**.

> **[mark-scheme]**
> **Mark allocation**
> 
> This answer is assessed using a point-marked approach.
> 
> - One mark for each valid point
> - Maximum 3 marks
> 
> **Alternative content**
> 
> The answer above is just one example of how to respond to this question. Other information that could be used includes:
> 
> - One volcano is in the sea, on a separate island (Surtsey)
> - Any other suitable response
